title: Asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI-CDG) initially mistaken for excessive alcohol consumption.

screening.reason: The abstract links elevated carbohydrate‑deficient transferrin, a glycan biomarker, to asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency, a glycosylation disorder, providing quantitative glycan data and disease association.

entities.evidence_sentence: In a routine company health check-up, a 32-year-old woman presented a highly elevated serum level of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT), a biomarker for excessive alcohol consumption.

The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.

The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.
The abnormal 'type-1' transferrin glycoform pattern indicated a defect in N-glycan assembly occurring in congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG), a family of rare inherited metabolic disorders.

evidence_sentences.sentence: In a routine company health check-up, a 32-year-old woman presented a highly elevated serum level of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT), a biomarker for excessive alcohol consumption.

The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.
The abnormal 'type-1' transferrin glycoform pattern indicated a defect in N-glycan assembly occurring in congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG), a family of rare inherited metabolic disorders.

Probing for the underlying enzyme defect(s) using cultured skin fibroblasts demonstrated normal activity of phosphomannomutase, whereas the activity of phosphomannose isomerase (MPI) was reduced (0.64 mU/mg protein, reference 2.1-6.9), pointing to CDG of the MPI subtype (formerly called CDG-Ib).

title: Abundance-ratio-based semiquantitative analysis of site-specific N-linked glycopeptides present in the plasma of hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

screening.reason: The study identifies site‑specific fucosylated vs non‑fucosylated N‑linked glycans on vitronectin in HCC plasma, a clear glycan biomarker linked to disease. However, the abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics (e.g., p‑values, fold‑change, AUC) and detailed sample information, so full text is needed.

title: Glycation of the complement regulatory protein CD59 is a novel biomarker for glucose handling in humans.

screening.reason: Glycated CD59 (GCD59) in circulating blood is shown to correlate with HbA1c, predict OGTT response, and decrease with insulin therapy, providing a clear glycan biomarker for glucose handling in diabetes.
